title: A race for survival.
voice: China’s EV boom became a race for survival. A 2018 report put the number of electric-vehicle manufacturers at nearly five hundred.

title: BIG FUNDING. UNCERTAIN OUTCOMES.
voice: The capital commitments were enormous. Reported funding ranged from around eight point four billion yuan at Byton to around thirty-five billion at WM Motor. These figures describe funding, not cash losses.

title: Investment is only the beginning.
voice: Byton reportedly raised eight point four billion yuan without reaching mass production. Saleen received six point six billion in state-backed investment, yet reportedly sold just thirty-one Maimai cars.

title: 2014. A new industry opens.
voice: Around 2014, policy support and Tesla’s patent pledge helped fuel optimism. Entrants from technology, property and consumer electronics saw an opportunity. But entering the market was easier than mastering automotive manufacturing.

title: Two sources. One ambition.
voice: Venture capital backed ambitious growth stories. Local governments offered land, facilities and industrial funding, seeking jobs, tax revenue and economic development. But financing a factory was only the beginning.

title: Funding is not manufacturing.
voice: For some startups, fundraising moved faster than manufacturing readiness. Launch events promised the future, while production schedules slipped. Suppliers, quality control and working capital remained critical.

title: Shutdowns. Restructurings.
voice: From 2020, shutdowns and restructurings exposed the risks. A review of fifteen troubled EV firms put disclosed funding above one hundred billion yuan.

title: WHEN LIABILITIES OUTWEIGH ASSETS
voice: WM Motor illustrates the balance-sheet risk. Reported liabilities were about five times book assets. Asset coverage was under twenty percent. Book values do not guarantee recovery.

title: SCALE OF THE SURVIVORS
voice: By 2025, surviving brands had reached substantial scale. The selected delivery figures show very different volumes. But deliveries alone do not establish profitability, or guarantee a supplier’s long-term continuity.

title: Price pressure. Margin pressure.
voice: Price competition puts margins under pressure. The next test is sustaining the business behind each vehicle.

title: Three tests for EV business.
voice: Three lessons: verify manufacturing capability, examine funding obligations, and assess margins alongside sales scale. Supplier continuity matters.
